articles.text: LÍNJŪ: Lín Dàjiě, xǐ yīfu na!
NEIGHBOR: Older Sister Lín, doing your laundry?
LÍN DÀJIĚ: Bù xǐ zěnme bàn? Shàng bānde shàng bān, shàng xuéde shàng xué, jiālide shìr hái bú shi dōu děi wǒ zuò!
OLDER SISTER LÍN: If I didn't do it what would we do? Everyone is either at the office or at school — don't I have to do all the housework in the end!
LÍNJŪ: Háizimen dōu máng, yǒu nín zài jiā, gěi tāmen bāng bù shǎo mángr.
NEIGHBOR: Your children are all busy, but you're at home helping them out a lot.
LÍN DÀJIĚ: Āi, niánji dà le, zuòbuliǎo duōshao shìr le!
OLDER SISTER LÍN: (Sigh) I'm getting old, I can't do very much any more!
LÍNJŪ: Wǒ kàn, nín érxífur zài jiāde shíhour, yě bāng nín zuò bù shǎo shì a.
NEIGHBOR: I see that when your daughter-in-law is home she helps you do a lot of things too.
LÍN DÀJIĚ: Nǐ shuōde yìdiǎnr yě bú cuò. Wǒ nèige érxífur bǐ wǒ érzi hǎoduō le, yí dào jiā, yòu zuò fàn, yòu xǐ yīfu, yòu shōushi wūzi. Āi! Kěxī wǒ bù néng shénme shìr dōu kào tā ya.

OLDER SISTER LÍN: You're absolutely right. That daughter-in-law of mine is much better than my son. As soon as she gets to the house, she cooks and washes and straightens up the room. (Sigh) It's too bad I can't depend on her for everything.
LÍNJŪ: Wèishénme ne?
NEIGHBOR: Why not?
LÍN DÀJIĚ: Rénjia duō máng! Yíge yuè cái néng huí jiā yícì.
OLDER SISTER LÍN: She's so busy! She can only come home once a month.
LÍNJŪ: Nà tā bù néng zài nín jiāli zhùxialai ma?
NEIGHBOR: Well, can't she move in with you?
LÍN DÀJIĚ: Bù xíng a! Wūzi tài xiǎo! Érxífur huílaile, ràng tā zhù zài nǎr?
OLDER SISTER LÍN: That wouldn't do! The house is too small! If my daughter-in-law came back, where would I have her stay?
LÍNJŪ: Shì a! Yàoshi yǒu fángzi, yìjiā rén zhù zài yíkuàir, hùxiāng bāngmángr, nà yǒu duō hǎo! Duì le, tīng wǒ nǚér shuō, tāmen xuéxiào nèibianr gàile hǎo duō xīn fángzi.

NEIGHBOR: Yes! If you had enough housing, how nice it would be to have the whole family living together and helping each other. Oh yes — I hear from my daughter that a lot of new buildings have been built over by their school.
LÍN DÀJIĚ: Fángzi wèntí shi ge dà shìr, zhèngfǔ bú huì bù guǎn. Yǒule xīn fángzi, zánmen jiù hǎo le.
OLDER SISTER LÍN: The housing problem is a big thing; the government wouldn't ignore it. After we get some new housing we'll be all right.
LÍNJŪ: Kě bú shi ma! Dàole nèige shíhour, nín jiù bú yòng dānxīn le. Nín gēn nín érxífur yídìng néng bǎ zhèige jiā nòngde shūshufufude.
NEIGHBOR: That's for sure! When that time comes you won't have to worry any more. I'm sure you and your daughter-in-law will be able to make a very comfortable home.
LÍN DÀJIĚ: Shì a! Nà jiù hǎo le!
OLDER SISTER LÍN: Yes! Then everything will be all right!
LÍNJŪ: Hǎo, Lín Dàjiě, bù zǎo le, wǒ yě gāi huí jiā zuò fàn qu le. Yǒu shíjiān zài liáo a.
NEIGHBOR: All right, Older Sister Lín, it's getting late, and I should really be going back home to fix dinner. We'll chat some more when we have time.
LÍN DÀJIĚ: Méi shìr jiù lái zuòzuo. Màn zǒu a!
OLDER SISTER LÍN: Stop in sometime when you're not busy. Take care!
